turns.reply:
The fix is in `fastapi/_compat/v2.py`, and I submitted it as a one-file patch. Nested models that are also used as top-level input or response types are no longer dropped from the generated definitions, so both `Sub-Input` and `Sub-Output` now appear when needed.

The cause was a filter in `get_definitions` that excluded any flat model whose type was already a top-level field type. In that case the nested model's validation schema was never generated, so input references pointed at a missing definition. I removed that filter so every flat model is included, matching the pre-filter behaviour. The existing `tests/test_openapi_separate_input_output_schemas.py` passes (6 tests), and a manual repro with a nested model that is also a response model produces the expected separate input and output schemas.

I did not confirm this against the exact hidden tests for issue #14247.
